subject: Request: Azure Marketplace pricing exception & distributor commission reconciliation
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Susan Hwang <susan.hwang@cloudprocure.com>, procurement@edenhealth.com
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Azure Marketplace pricing exception & distributor commission reconciliation

Hi Susan / Jun—

Thanks for the demo last week. Per our executive sponsor's ask, EdenHealth is looking to push a firm commit across Azure Marketplace but needs one additional concession to match a competing offer: a 12-month blended list-price floor with a distributor commission passback at 9%.

We reviewed internally and need to confirm two things before we can sign:
- Can Azure private offer be configured with a blended list for the committed SKUs (reserved capacity + metered node hours)?
- Will Redwood recognize a 9% distributor/backchannel commission in the invoice path (we'd offset via a passback credit)?

I've attached a spreadsheet with the proposed numbers. For the contract, the customer is asking for a clause that ties the first true-up to the commit anniversary (not calendar month) and a short audit window for distributor evidence (30 days).

Next steps I propose:
1) Susan — confirm whether CloudProcure (distributor) can provide the 9% evidence file and format (example attached).
2) Irene — can Legal & RevOps vet a short audit window + invoice passback mechanics?
3) Ben/Camila — ops impact and whether this requires a dedicated SKU mapping in billing.

Appreciate quick feedback; customer is on a tight procurement timeline.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Cloud Marketplaces, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: edenhealth-pricing-proposal.xlsx (spreadsheet), commission-evidence-2026-06.csv (csv sample)

From: Susan Hwang <susan.hwang@cloudprocure.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, procurement@edenhealth.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Azure Marketplace pricing exception & distributor commission reconciliation

Thanks Marcus — quick note from CloudProcure side.

We can provide a monthlyized evidence export in CSV or JSON showing invoice-level passbacks tied to the EdenHealth order id. The 9% distributor commission is within our normal passback range; we just need the client PO and marketplace listing id. Example: commission-evidence-2026-06.csv (attached).

A couple clarifying asks from EdenHealth (cc'd Jun):
- The commit anniversary true-up: do you expect the first true-up to align with the signed date or the first consumption month?
- For blended list-price: are you expecting list-price floor + metered discounts applied at settlement or at invoice time?

Jun — noting the procurement questions; happy to jump on a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the evidence file if helpful.

Best,
Susan Hwang
Commercial Lead, CloudProcure
susan.hwang@cloudprocure.com

Attachment: commission-evidence-2026-06.csv

From: Jun Tanaka <j.tanaka@edenhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Susan Hwang <susan.hwang@cloudprocure.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 14:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Azure Marketplace pricing exception & distributor commission reconciliation

Marcus / Susan—

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Procurement intent: first true-up should align with the signed date (we want the anniversary to be predictable), and we prefer passback credits recorded at invoice settlement so our internal auditors can match credits against invoice lines.

One more ask: we need a short clause that allows EdenHealth to request a one-time independent verification of distributor evidence within 45 days of the first true-up. Not an ongoing audit program — just the option to validate once.

If Redwood can accept those mechanics (signed-date anniversary + settlement-level passbacks + 45-day independent verification option), we can move to signatures this month.

Jun Tanaka
Sr. Dir. Procurement, EdenHealth
j.tanaka@edenhealth.com

(On mobile)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Susan Hwang <susan.hwang@cloudprocure.com>, Jun Tanaka <j.tanaka@edenhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Azure Marketplace pricing exception & distributor commission reconciliation

Hi all — internal + external summary after Legal / RevOps chat. Quoting Jun above: signed-date anniversary + settlement-level passbacks + one-time independent verification within 45 days are reasonable with a few guardrails.

Proposed redlines we can accept:
- Contract language: first true-up aligned to the effective date (signed date).
- Passback mechanics: Redwood will accept distributor credit evidence for invoice settlement reconciliation; credits will be applied as a separate credit memo referencing the marketplace invoice id.
- Verification: EdenHealth may request one independent verification within 45 days of the first true-up; verification scope limited to the specific commission evidence files and invoice reconciliation for that true-up period. Any additional requests will be evaluated and may require a commercial fee.

Operational notes (Ben / Camila): to implement this cleanly we need a dedicated invoice tag (marketplace_passback_id) on our billing pipeline and a short mapping table for reserved SKU vs metered SKU so credits hit the correct line items. Ben — estimate effort and timeline? Camila — will ops require a one-off SKU mapping for EdenHealth?

If CloudProcure can confirm the format and provide a signed evidence sample, we can attach an exhibit to the PO and circulate the final terms (I attached a draft exception redline for your review).

Irene Choi
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-terms-exception-draft.pdf
